cover.album: Did you know that there’s a tunnel under Ocean Blvd

cards.headline: An album born from raw phone voice notes
cards.snippet: While making the album that contains "Kintsugi", Lana Del Rey dropped her usual world-building and tried what she called "automatic singing". She hummed whatever came to mind into her phone's voice notes app, with no prior writing. She sent those rough recordings to composer Drew Erickson, who added reverb to her vocals and built orchestral arrangements around them. The first song written for the album, "Fingertips", was made this way.
cards.context: Album: Did You Know That There's a Tunnel Under Ocean Blvd (2023).

cards.headline: "Kintsugi" holds her innermost thoughts
cards.snippet: Del Rey singled out "Kintsugi" and "Fingertips" when she described the album's songs. She called both "super long and wordy" and said they hold her innermost thoughts. They sit back to back on the album, and both are among its most personal and confessional moments.

cards.headline: The real tunnel behind the album's title
cards.snippet: The album's title points to the Jergins Tunnel, which runs beneath the Jergins Trust Building in Long Beach, California. It was built in 1927 and closed in 1967. Del Rey uses the forgotten tunnel as a symbol of her fear of being forgotten. That theme of memory and loss runs through the record that "Kintsugi" belongs to.
cards.context: Title story for the parent album.

cards.headline: The song's whole idea in one line
cards.snippet: “There is a crack in everything, that's how the light gets in”
cards.context: A Leonard Cohen lyric that matches the meaning of kintsugi, the Japanese art of mending broken pottery with gold.

replies.author: @matheussimoes3597
replies.text: I listen to Lana everyday, even I can still find out quotes like this that I've never truly noticed before

replies.author: @hetty9486
replies.text: I like to tell myself that Sir Leonard Cohen would have loved Lana's last albums

cards.headline: A Japanese fan on hearing her own word in a Lana song
cards.snippet: I’m Japanese and been her fan since 2013. I’m not really a nationalist, but it was a lovely surprise to know she made a song with a Japanese word, and the background behind the song is beautiful, thank you.
cards.context: Kintsugi is a Japanese word for repairing broken ceramics with gold.

replies.author: @TheKoolWhip
replies.text: Sometimes I will look into a single Japanese word (like Kintsugi) and 2 hours later I come up for air. Amazing culture. And song.

replies.author: @ironyelegy
replies.text: not gonna lie the specification that you're not a nationalist was relieving. love Japan and its people but you get what I mean. I share your overall enthusiasm as well :-)

cards.headline: Still mad about the Grammys
cards.snippet: How could this lose to Midnights
cards.context: The album was nominated for Album of the Year at the 66th Grammys, a category Taylor Swift's Midnights won. Fans still argue about it.

replies.author: @taka-taktak
replies.text: Same way TPAB lost to 1989. Grammys reward the most commercial not the most artistic.

cards.headline: A song that made a father and daughter cry together
cards.snippet: and he understood and broke down with me. We hugged and he said in my ear I miss them too.
cards.context: The commenter shared the lyrics with her dad, and verse 2 reminded both of his late parents.

replies.author: @TheAashnag123
replies.text: I wish I could have that moment with my dad.

cards.headline: Joy Zhang's acoustic take on Lana's "Kintsugi"
cards.snippet: Joy Zhang sings and plays the song in an acoustic arrangement, which she calls a difficult one to cover. She performs only part of the song.
